input.question: Before the advent of the light bulb/artificial light, was drinking primarily a daytime activity?
input.ground_truth: Well its not like before the invention of the lightbulb we were all fumbling around in the dark when night fell. Oil Lamps have been around for thousands of years and torches and roaring fires give off a fairly hefty amount of light easily illuminating a room. Just think of anytime you've been near a roaring fire and the light that comes off that.

Question: Before the advent of the light bulb/artificial light, was drinking primarily a daytime activity?

response.prediction:
Okay! Let’s imagine it together:

Before there were light bulbs and lamps that make light at night, people could only see well when the sun was up. So, after the sun went down and it got dark, it was really hard to see things clearly.

Because it was hard to see at night, most people didn’t want to do things like pour water into a cup or walk around with a glass. They were worried they might spill or bump into things. So, they mostly drank water or had their drinks during the day, when it was light outside.

At night, people usually just didn’t drink much, or they had a little water if they really needed it, but they didn’t make it a big part of their evening like we do now with our night lights on.

So, yes! Drinking was mostly a daytime thing before we had artificial light.
